title: Per-Invocation Spend Lens & Pricing Templater
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Design a compact, role-aware dashboard and export patterns for per-invocation (token-level) spend visibility. Deliver a low-friction UI that lets engineers and finance teams: filter by model/route/customer, view token-level attribution (prompt vs. completion vs. system), preview pricing rules (rate bands, SKUs, discounts), and export validated CSV/NDJSON payloads for chargeback and accounting. The design should balance density (engineering workflows) and explainability (finance audits) and include a pricing templater to preview invoice impact of routing/quantization changes.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma prototype for desktop and tablet showing: overview, detailed invocation row, expanded attribution drilldown, pricing templater modal, and export flow
Export formats: CSV (human-friendly) and NDJSON (chargeback-ready) with schema examples included in spec
Role-aware UX: toggle to switch between Engineer, Finance, and Platform Admin views with persisted column presets
Pricing templater: slider-driven volume & discount preview that updates per-invocation effective rate and total spend estimate
Engineering handoff: component specs, token-count microcopy, accessibility annotations, and interaction states documented
Usability sign-off: two roundtables with PM, Eng (runtime), and a finance stakeholder; top 3 usability issues addressed
comments: 2026-01-26 — Asha K: Initial discovery notes attached; finance wants per-customer rollups plus raw invocation downloads. Confirmed export schema requirements with Finance (Luca).

2026-02-10 — Marco D (Eng): KV cache and batching metadata are available but may increase payload size. We should allow a trimmed export that omits KV fields to keep CSV <10MB for typical queries.

2026-03-05 — Finance feedback (Luca Rossi): CSV must include stable identifiers for customer and route; add ledger-friendly amount fields (unit_rate, discount_applied, applied_rate, gross_tokens).
2026-03-11 — Accessibility check (Sofia P): color contrasts pass; add keyboard shortcut for expand/collapse rows; ensure screen reader reads 'attribution: prompt X tokens, completion Y tokens'.
reviewer_feedback: PM (Liang C): Good balance between density and clarity. Ask Eng to validate export performance and file size limits before dev start.
Eng (Marco D): Implementation notes — server-side CSV streaming recommended; NDJSON must include routing_policy_id and model_variant_id for downstream chargeback mapping.
Finance (Luca R): Add sample invoice mapping in Confluence that demonstrates how templater outputs map to P&L lines. Prefer named rate bands in exports for audit ease.
